name: hard-blink
concept: Opacity snaps instantly between fully visible and fully hidden, with no fade in between. Use it for a strict binary indicator, like a state that is simply on or off.

name: strict-strobe
concept: Opacity snaps between fully visible and nearly invisible, holding each state before the next hard cut. Use it where the element must stay faintly present instead of vanishing completely.

name: bare-blink
concept: Opacity cuts sharply between full strength and a dimmed half state, never fading through the middle. Use it for a mild version of a hard blink that still reads as interrupted.

name: crisp-toggle
concept: Opacity snaps on and off twice as often as a normal blink, with each cut equally sharp. Use it for a fast, rigid toggle that reads as mechanical rather than organic.

name: instant-flicker
concept: Opacity drops to zero for a brief instant, then snaps straight back, all within a short cycle. Use it for a very fast, clean toggle that feels almost too quick to track.

name: square-blink
concept: Opacity holds fully visible for most of the cycle, then cuts sharply to a low floor for a short stretch. Use it for a steady presence with a brief, unmistakable interruption.

name: shutter-blink
concept: Opacity stays fully visible and drops out for only an instant, like a camera shutter closing once per cycle. Use it for a subtle, mostly steady element with one sharp beat.

name: failing-bulb
concept: Opacity dips at uneven points and depths, mimicking a fluorescent tube about to die. Use it to suggest a faulty or aging light source rather than a deliberate signal.

name: dying-fluorescent
concept: Opacity stutters through long steady stretches broken by sudden uneven drops, like a fluorescent tube losing its charge. Use it for a slower, more drawn-out failing light effect.

name: loose-connection
concept: Opacity holds steady, then drops to near black for a sudden brief instant at unpredictable points. Use it to suggest a bad electrical contact rather than a constant flicker.

name: static-flicker
concept: Opacity jitters in small rapid steps throughout the cycle, like visual noise or static interference. Use it for a nervous, unstable presence rather than a slow failing light.

name: faulty-wire
concept: Opacity mostly stays near full, but drops all the way to zero for one unpredictable stretch per cycle. Use it for a rare, jarring total dropout amid otherwise normal visibility.

name: candle-flicker
concept: Opacity and scale waver gently and unevenly around a high resting point, like a flame reacting to soft air currents. Use it for a warm, living flicker rather than a cold electrical fault.

name: old-tv-flicker
concept: Opacity twitches in fast, small, uneven increments throughout the cycle, like a television losing signal. Use it for a dated, glitchy screen effect.

name: glitch-flicker
concept: Opacity jumps abruptly between full and zero at irregular points, with no smooth transition, like a digital signal error. Use it for a broken, glitchy attention cue.

name: haunted-flicker
concept: Opacity holds steady for a long stretch, then suddenly dips hard and unevenly before settling again. Use it for an eerie, unpredictable presence rather than a rhythmic blink.

name: gentle-fade-flicker
concept: Opacity eases slowly and smoothly between full strength and a slightly dimmed state. Use it for a calm, barely noticeable flicker that will not distract from nearby content.

name: soft-dim-flicker
concept: Opacity eases slowly toward a noticeably dimmer floor before rising back to full. Use it for a slightly deeper gentle flicker than a barely there variant, while staying smooth.

name: faint-flicker
concept: Opacity dips twice per cycle by slightly different amounts, both times gently and smoothly. Use it for a soft flicker with a little more texture than a single smooth dip.

name: subtle-dim-pulse
concept: Opacity eases very slowly toward a deep dim and back, over a long, calm cycle. Use it for the slowest and deepest of the gentle fade flickers, for a quietly dramatic effect.

name: whisper-flicker
concept: Opacity dips quickly to a soft floor, then rises back slowly and smoothly, giving an asymmetric, breath like rhythm. Use it for a gentle flicker with a distinct inhale exhale feel.

name: low-flicker
concept: Opacity eases smoothly and quickly to a mild dim, then holds briefly before recovering. Use it for a short, gentle flicker on the faster end of the slow fade family.

name: urgent-strobe
concept: Opacity snaps between full and off very quickly and steadily, reading as an urgent alert. Use it when attention is needed right away, such as a critical warning.

name: rapid-strobe
concept: Opacity switches between full and off at the fastest pace in the strobe family, almost too quick to follow. Use it sparingly, for the most urgent possible cue.

name: panic-strobe
concept: Opacity flashes quickly on, then stays off for a longer stretch of each short cycle. Use it for an urgent strobe with a jittery, uneven duty cycle that feels more frantic.

name: emergency-strobe
concept: Opacity strobes rapidly between full and a low but visible floor, never fully vanishing. Use it for an urgent cue that must still remain legible, like emergency lighting.

name: alarm-strobe
concept: Opacity fires two rapid flashes within each short cycle before repeating, like a warning light double pulsing. Use it for an urgent strobe with a distinct double flash texture.

name: warning-strobe
concept: Opacity strobes quickly between full and a faint glow, at a slightly gentler pace than the fastest strobes. Use it for an urgent but marginally less intense warning cue.

name: double-blink
concept: Opacity flashes off twice in quick succession, then holds steady for a longer pause before repeating. Use it for a notification cue that reads as two short taps.

name: text-notification-blink
concept: Opacity fades down and back up twice in quick succession with soft edges, then rests before repeating. Use it for a gentler double blink suited to message notifications.

name: two-tap-flicker
concept: Opacity dips to a visible floor twice in a row, never fully vanishing, then pauses at full strength. Use it for a double blink that stays legible throughout.

name: paired-flash
concept: Opacity flashes off twice with a clear gap between the two flashes, then rests for a longer stretch. Use it when the two beats of a double blink should feel distinctly separate.

name: heartbeat-blink
concept: Opacity dips twice quickly, the second dip a little deeper than the first, then rests, echoing a heartbeat's lub dub. Use it for a lively double blink notification.

name: quick-double-flicker
concept: Opacity fires two very fast, tight blinks back to back, then pauses briefly before repeating. Use it for the quickest and tightest of the double blink patterns.

name: blink-blink-pause
concept: Opacity snaps off twice sharply, then holds fully visible for a long, calm pause before the pattern repeats. Use it when the rest between double blinks should dominate the cycle.

name: electric-flicker
concept: Opacity dips unevenly while brightness rises slightly at each dip, suggesting a small electrical surge. Use it for a flicker with an extra charged, electric quality.

name: charged-flicker
concept: Opacity and brightness both climb briefly at irregular points before settling back down, like static building up. Use it for a flicker that feels like it is gathering charge.

name: static-charge
concept: Brightness leads the motion with a small steady pulse while opacity dips only slightly. Use it when the electrical feel should read mainly through light intensity, not visibility.

name: power-surge-flicker
concept: Opacity drops deeply and unevenly at one point in the cycle while brightness spikes right after, like a power surge followed by a dim recovery. Use it for a dramatic electrical fault.

name: live-wire-flicker
concept: Opacity and brightness jitter together in small fast increments, like a live wire sparking continuously. Use it for a fast, nervy electrical texture.

name: voltage-flicker
concept: Brightness swells and fades slowly while opacity holds mostly steady with only a mild dip. Use it for a slow, moody electrical shimmer rather than a fast fault.

name: current-flicker
concept: Opacity and brightness both flicker in short irregular bursts spread unevenly across the cycle, like current running inconsistently through a wire. Use it for a textured electrical fault.

name: dramatic-flash
concept: Opacity starts dim, then flashes brightly to full just once before settling. Use it for a one-time dramatic reveal, such as confirming a rare event.

name: sudden-flash
concept: Opacity and brightness both spike together once, from a dim resting state to an overexposed peak, before settling back to normal. Use it for a rare, high impact one-time alert.

name: quiet-pulse
concept: Opacity eases smoothly between two visible levels, never approaching zero. Use it for a quiet, always present cue that signals gentle ongoing activity.

name: standby-pulse
concept: Opacity eases gently between a near full level and a moderate floor, never dimming too far. Use it for a standby cue that reads as idle but ready.

name: idle-glimmer
concept: Opacity eases slowly between two mid range levels, keeping the element present but understated. Use it for a low key idle indicator that avoids drawing too much attention.

name: steady-alive-pulse
concept: Opacity eases between full strength and a high floor, dipping only a little to stay clearly alive without fading much. Use it for a confident, steady presence cue.

name: resting-pulse
concept: Opacity eases between a moderate level and a dimmer one, resting well below full strength throughout. Use it for a cue that should look calm and low energy, but never fully fade.

name: low-power-pulse
concept: Opacity eases very slowly between a dim mid level and a lower floor, suggesting reduced energy. Use it for a slow, conservative pulse that reads as running on low power.
